players.product: circuit protection (eFuses, TVS) and power semiconductors for datacenter power

quarterly_data.signal: Second-quarter net sales of $739 million, up 20% year-over-year and 14% organically, above expectations; the Basler acquisition contributed approximately 6% to sales growth and foreign exchange was a 1% tailwind. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 23.6%, up 220 basis points on volume leverage, favorable mix and operational execution; adjusted diluted EPS was $4.19, up 47%. Operating cash flow was $146 million and free cash flow $127 million, up 75%; the quarter ended with $628 million of cash and consolidated net leverage of approximately 0.8 turns.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales $739 million (+20% YoY, +14% organic); adjusted EBITDA margin 23.6% (+220 basis points); adjusted EPS $4.19 (+47%); free cash flow $127 million

quarterly_data.signal: Third-quarter outlook: net sales of $780 million to $800 million, 26% growth versus the prior year at the midpoint, made up of 21% organic growth, a 6% contribution from the Basler acquisition and a 1% FX headwind; adjusted diluted EPS of $4.85 to $5.05, 68% growth at the midpoint; adjusted effective tax rate of 23% to 24%. CFO: the guide reflects continued healthy demand across several key markets, supported by a strong backlog and increased customer traction; incremental margins come from volume leverage, operational execution and mix, with passives and protection having very high flow-through.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 net sales $780 million to $800 million (26% growth at midpoint, 21% organic); adjusted EPS $4.85 to $5.05 (68% growth at midpoint)

quarterly_data.signal: Long-term targets reaffirmed: CFO pointed to the 2030 targets of $4.5 billion in revenue and $1.1 billion in adjusted EBITDA laid out at the May Investor Day; CEO said the company is on track to the model laid out at Investor Day and that second-quarter performance and second-half momentum reinforce confidence in the long-term growth and profitability framework.
quarterly_data.figure: 2030 targets: $4.5 billion revenue, $1.1 billion adjusted EBITDA

quarterly_data.signal: Bookings and design wins: the company entered the third quarter with record bookings — Q2 bookings were a company-wide record — and a book-to-bill 'well north of 1.0', broad across data center, industrial verticals, diversified industrials and HVAC. Design wins were up double digits in each market through the first half. CFO: organic growth went from 9% in Q1 to 14% in Q2 and a 21% midpoint guide for Q3, and the strong bookings support that guide (exact booking numbers are not disclosed).
quarterly_data.figure: record Q2 bookings; book-to-bill well north of 1.0; organic growth 9% (Q1), 14% (Q2), 21% guided (Q3)

quarterly_data.signal: Data center: CEO said data center remained a leading contributor to growth in the computing, communications and diversified industrial (CCDI) market, and the CFO said it was the fastest-growing market in the quarter and the first half; management expects it to keep growing through the second half of 2026. CEO: this year's data center revenue is largely from low-voltage architectures; high-voltage architectures are expected 'probably in 2027 and beyond', with very low volume proof-of-concept shipments today that will ramp later.
quarterly_data.figure: high-voltage data center architectures expected probably in 2027 and beyond; very low volume proof-of-concept shipments today

quarterly_data.signal: High-voltage data center content: CEO said data center design wins more than doubled compared with a year before, heavily focused on the higher-voltage architectures, and the pipeline has heavy strength there. CFO: the content opportunity is two to four times higher in high voltage versus low voltage today in terms of revenue, and management is 'pretty confident' in the 25% to 30% CAGR over the next five years laid out for its data center markets.
quarterly_data.figure: data center design wins more than doubled YoY; high-voltage content two to four times low-voltage; 25% to 30% data center CAGR over five years

quarterly_data.signal: Data center battery backup design win: in the quarter Littelfuse was awarded a significant program with an unnamed leader in battery energy storage and power supply applications; its fast-acting TLS fuses optimize performance of battery backup units for data center markets. CEO: the win and the strategic partnership position the company for the expansion of high-voltage battery storage for both data center and grid-scale markets.

Power semiconductors: demand strengthened in the quarter with good bookings and orders, contributing to improved growth and profitability, and CEO sees continued momentum into the third quarter, where power semiconductors will be a strong contributor to incrementals. The business is being refocused on high-power, high-value applications with a differentiated right to win through a multiyear portfolio rationalization and footprint optimization. Example: a design win with an unnamed leading fusion-power player using Littelfuse high-voltage IGBTs and diodes to manage the stored energy that drives the fusion reaction, with 4.5 kV operation in a compact footprint; shipments begin in the third quarter as the customer builds its first prototype reactor.
quarterly_data.figure: 4.5 kV IGBT/diode solution; fusion customer shipments begin in Q3

quarterly_data.signal: Allen, Texas fab closure: the power semiconductor manufacturing facility in Allen, Texas, announced for closure earlier this year, is slated to close in 2027 as an early step in footprint rationalization. CFO: it is a make-versus-buy decision to simplify the operational footprint, reduce lead times and improve the cost structure; savings are expected in the back half of 2027 and the closure should enhance 2027 Electronics segment profitability. CEO: other actions will follow over time.
quarterly_data.figure: Allen, Texas power semiconductor fab to close in 2027; savings in back half of 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Electronics Products segment: sales up 21% year-over-year with 20% organic growth; passive products delivered strong growth and semiconductor products benefited from continued protection strength and improved power semiconductor demand, with higher demand in data center, diversified industrials and transportation. Segment adjusted EBITDA margin was 26.3%, up 470 basis points.
quarterly_data.figure: Electronics sales +21% YoY (+20% organic); adjusted EBITDA margin 26.3% (+470 basis points)

quarterly_data.signal: Industrial segment: sales up 52% year-over-year, 16% organic, on data center, industrial automation and construction demand plus a faster-than-expected HVAC recovery; Basler contributed approximately 36% of the segment's growth. HVAC had been down four straight quarters and grew year-over-year for the first time since the first half of 2025. Basler is performing ahead of expectations and now is expected to contribute approximately $135 million to $140 million of revenue in 2026 (above the prior outlook) and $0.25 to $0.30 of EPS; CEO said Basler drives significant momentum in grid and utility infrastructure, alongside energy demand from grid modernization, utility investment and renewables. Segment adjusted EBITDA margin was 22.6%, up 50 basis points.
quarterly_data.figure: Industrial sales +52% YoY (+16% organic); Basler 2026 revenue $135 million to $140 million, EPS $0.25 to $0.30; adjusted EBITDA margin 22.6%

quarterly_data.signal: Transportation Products segment: sales up 2% year-over-year, 1% organic, driven by stronger commercial vehicle volumes in truck, construction and agricultural equipment; passenger vehicle organic sales declined 2% on lower global production and continued sensor product declines; adjusted EBITDA margin 18.6%. CEO said passenger vehicle growth came from content expansion and share gains. Design win: an integrated current sensor and MEGA Fuse solution with up to a 700 amp protection rating for a leading transportation customer's light truck and commercial vehicle platform, more than $20 million in annual revenue opportunity.
quarterly_data.figure: Transportation sales +2% YoY (+1% organic); passenger vehicle organic -2%; adjusted EBITDA margin 18.6%; design win more than $20 million annual revenue opportunity

quarterly_data.signal: End-market breadth and share: CEO sees broad-based momentum, including diversified industrial (medical, aerospace and defense); consumer electronics sales declined and represent less than 10% of company sales. Channel inventory is normal in weeks, POS and POA are both growing strongly, and apart from some normalization where inventories were low, management views demand as real end demand. CEO believes the company is gaining share on balance, largely through design position rather than opportunistic share; CFO said the company is focused on operational execution to fulfil customer demand.
quarterly_data.figure: consumer electronics less than 10% of sales; channel inventory normal in weeks
